title: Proper direct-image constructibility over a Noetherian base
statement: Fix universes u and u+1, a prime ell, a field k in universe u with ringChar(k) different from ell, schemes Z,Y in universe u, a morphism aY:Y→Spec(k), a Noetherian Y, and a proper p:Z→Y. Let Λ be a commutative condensed ring object, with its specified multiplication, having IsEllAdicFinitenessCoefficient ell Λ: a finite normed Q_ell extension, the induced ring of integers of a finite embedded extension, the finite-subextension-valued algebraic closure, or the closed unit ball of a finite normed extension. Put Λ_T=p_T^*Λ and D_T=D(Mod(Λ_T)), with the actual total right derived functor Rp_* [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Constructibility means stratified local finite presentation [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. The coefficient certification is the four-constructor class in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.RingObjects.Condensed.FinitenessCoefficient, with its monoid-object index, rather than a new coefficient construction. For every bounded K in D_Z whose cohomology module objects are constructible, and every integer q, H^q(Rp_*K) is a constructible Λ_Y-module object. This assertion imposes no upper bound on the cohomology of Rp_*K. No finite-type or separatedness assumption is imposed on aY, and k may have characteristic zero.

source.place: Integral and rational proper finiteness, constructibility clauses; Bhatt--Scholze 6.7.2 and Remark 6.8.15.

proof.text: For a proper morphism between Noetherian schemes, use the identity open immersion compactification. Compact-support constructibility therefore gives constructibility of ordinary etale direct-image cohomology for bounded constructible finite coefficients. A uniform finite fibre-dimension bound and proper torsion cohomological dimension give boundedness. The etale/pro-etale derived comparison transports this to ordinary pro-etale finite-field modules, where boundedness also gives finite Tor amplitude. The already proved source finiteTorAmplitude_of_boundedConstructible_of_field and torAmplitudeIn_mapDerivedCategory_iff supply field Tor amplitude and its comparison; no appeal is made to the separate abstract field-stage theorem. Reuse the proved private ProEtale.etale_cd from Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.FiniteProperClassicalCoproducts for the proper torsion bound; its proof combines the recorded torsion, forgetful and single-object comparison inputs.

Use the established finite discrete coefficient encoding and its constructibility, compactification and tensor compatibility to transport the finite-field bounded constructible and finite Tor result to internal module objects. Reuse the proved private ProEtale.ordinary_constructible_iff from Sheaf.Paper.LocalizingClosureCtfEqualsBc to identify the ordinary constructibility predicates; its elementary cover-index comparison includes empty covers and arbitrary small index universes.

For the actual continuous integer coefficient ring, the residue quotient is a finite field since the chosen uniformizer generates the maximal ideal of the extension DVR. Apply the internal residue criterion to the source, the finite-field result to its residue reduction, and the internal direct-image-limits theorem to identify the target reduction and preserve derived completeness. The target residue criterion proves bounded constant-model constructibility. The isomorphism-invariance predicates supplied by the finite-Tor well-definedness theorem justify transport of the residue comparison.

Identify the integer coefficient presentations by explicit continuous ring isomorphisms. The lattice coefficient integers and the extension integers differ only by WithAbs; for a normed finite extension the spectral norm agrees with the given norm, so the valuation ring identifies with its closed unit ball. Postcomposition gives inverse continuous-function sheaf maps and hence ring-object isomorphisms. Transport constructibility through scalar restriction and the derived direct-image comparison, using the established local-finite-presentation/constant-model comparison.

For continuous finite rational coefficients, choose an integral bounded constructible model. Its proper image has constructible cohomology by the integral result. The proved integral scalar/direct-image comparison and exact scalar extension identify its localized cohomology with that of the rational image. For the condensed algebraic closure, descend the input to a finite intermediate field, apply that rational result and use the bounded-below scalar/direct-image comparison. Finally case-split the four constructors of IsEllAdicFinitenessCoefficient, keeping the original theorem signature.

proof_origin.place: Bhatt--Scholze 6.7.1--6.7.2 and 6.8.15; finite etale finiteness, internal residue and direct-image-limits criteria, then integral models and scalar extension.

theorem properLowerStar_constructible_cohomology_ellAdic
    (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    (Λ : Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) Ab.{u + 1})
    [MonObj Λ] [IsCommMonObj Λ] [IsEllAdicFinitenessCoefficient ℓ Λ]
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [Fact (ringChar k ≠ ℓ)]
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsNoetherian Y]
    (p : Z ⟶ Y) [IsProper p]
    (K : DerivedCategory (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology Z) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj Λ Z)))
    (hK : boundedConstructible (condensedRingObj Λ Z) K) :
    ∀ q : ℤ, IsConstructibleModuleObject (condensedRingObj Λ Y)
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj (R((p)_*⟦Λ⟧).obj K))
